title: Goa
text: Goa is India's beach state on the west coast. Best time: November to February (dry, 25-32C). Monsoon June-September brings heavy rain; many beach shacks close. North Goa (Baga, Calangute, Anjuna) is lively with nightlife; South Goa (Palolem, Agonda, Colva) is quieter. Old Goa has Portuguese-era churches like Basilica of Bom Jesus (UNESCO). Nearest airports: Dabolim (GOI) and Manohar International (GOX, Mopa). Budget: 2500-6000 INR/day for mid-range. Scooter rental ~400 INR/day.

title: Kerala
text: Kerala in the south is known for backwaters, hill stations and Ayurveda. Alleppey (Alappuzha) houseboat cruises cost 7000-15000 INR/night for a couple. Munnar has tea plantations, best September-March. Kochi (Fort Kochi) has Chinese fishing nets and Kathakali shows. Varkala has cliff beaches. Best time overall: October to March. Monsoon June-August is popular for Ayurvedic treatments. Airports: Kochi (COK), Trivandrum (TRV), Calicut (CCJ).

title: Rajasthan
text: Rajasthan is the land of forts and palaces. Jaipur (Pink City): Amber Fort, Hawa Mahal, City Palace. Udaipur: lakes, City Palace, Lake Pichola boat ride. Jodhpur: Mehrangarh Fort, blue city. Jaisalmer: golden fort and Thar desert camel safaris at Sam sand dunes. Best time: October to March; summers exceed 45C. Typical 7-day circuit: Jaipur (2) - Jodhpur (2) - Jaisalmer (1) - Udaipur (2). Pushkar Camel Fair happens in November.

title: Golden Triangle
text: The Golden Triangle covers Delhi, Agra and Jaipur, roughly 5-6 days. Delhi to Agra by Gatimaan Express takes about 1h40m; by road via Yamuna Expressway ~3.5h. Taj Mahal is closed on Fridays; sunrise visit recommended. Foreign tourist Taj entry ~1100 INR (plus 200 for main mausoleum), Indians ~50 INR. Agra to Jaipur by road ~4.5h, stop at Fatehpur Sikri. Best time: October to March.

title: Himachal and Ladakh
text: Himachal Pradesh: Manali, Shimla, Dharamshala/McLeod Ganj, Spiti Valley. Best March-June and September-November; winter brings snow (Dec-Feb) good for snow lovers. Ladakh (Leh): best June to September; Manali-Leh and Srinagar-Leh highways open roughly June-October. Acclimatize 48 hours in Leh due to altitude 3500m to avoid AMS. Inner Line Permit needed for Nubra, Pangong, Tso Moriri for Indians; Protected Area Permit for foreigners. Rohtang Pass requires permit from Manali.

title: Northeast India
text: Northeast includes Meghalaya (Shillong, Cherrapunji living root bridges, Dawki clear river), Assam (Kaziranga one-horned rhino, open Nov-April), Sikkim (Gangtok, Tsomgo Lake, North Sikkim needs permit), Arunachal (Tawang; Inner Line Permit required for Indians, PAP for foreigners). Best time October to April. Nearest hub airport: Guwahati (GAU), Bagdogra (IXB) for Sikkim.

title: Varanasi and spiritual India
text: Varanasi on the Ganges is one of the oldest living cities. Ganga Aarti at Dashashwamedh Ghat every evening around 6-7 PM. Sunrise boat ride costs ~300-800 INR. Sarnath (Buddhist site) is 10 km away. Rishikesh is the yoga capital with river rafting (Sept-June). Amritsar Golden Temple offers free langar meals; Wagah border ceremony in evening. Bodh Gaya is where Buddha attained enlightenment.

title: Visa and entry
text: Most nationalities can apply for an Indian e-Visa online at indianvisaonline.gov.in: e-Tourist visa for 30 days, 1 year or 5 years. Apply at least 4 days before arrival. Passport must be valid for 6 months with 2 blank pages. Nepal and Bhutan citizens do not need a visa. Pakistani nationals and some others must apply via embassy. Register on arrival is not needed for e-Tourist up to 180 days.

title: Getting around India
text: Trains: book on IRCTC; classes 1A, 2A, 3A (AC), Sleeper (SL). Book 60 days ahead (advance reservation period); Tatkal quota opens one day before at 10 AM (AC) and 11 AM (non-AC). Vande Bharat are fast chair-car trains. Domestic flights: IndiGo, Air India, Akasa, SpiceJet. Uber and Ola work in major cities; use prepaid taxis at airports. Metro systems in Delhi, Mumbai, Bangalore, Kolkata, Chennai, Hyderabad.

title: Safety, health and money
text: Drink bottled or filtered water; avoid ice from unknown sources. Recommended vaccines: Hepatitis A, Typhoid; consult a doctor. Carry mosquito repellent for dengue/malaria in monsoon. Emergency number: 112. Women travellers: dress modestly at religious sites, prefer prepaid/app taxis at night. Currency is Indian Rupee (INR); UPI payments widely used, foreigners can use UPI One World wallet. ATMs common; carry cash in rural areas. Tipping 5-10% in restaurants.

title: Food and culture
text: Regional cuisine: North - butter chicken, chole bhature, parathas (Delhi, Amritsar). South - dosa, idli, sambar, Kerala fish curry, Chettinad, Hyderabadi biryani. West - Gujarati thali, vada pav (Mumbai), Goan fish curry. East - Bengali fish, rosogolla, momos in Northeast. Many restaurants are vegetarian. Remove shoes before entering temples and homes. Major festivals: Diwali (Oct/Nov), Holi (March), Durga Puja (Kolkata, Sept/Oct), Onam (Kerala, Aug/Sept).

title: Mumbai, Karnataka and Tamil Nadu
text: Mumbai: Gateway of India, Marine Drive, Elephanta Caves (ferry, closed Monday), Colaba. Karnataka: Hampi ruins (UNESCO, best Oct-Feb), Coorg coffee hills, Mysore Palace (Dasara festival), Bangalore. Tamil Nadu: Chennai, Mahabalipuram shore temple, Pondicherry French quarter, Madurai Meenakshi temple, Ooty and Kodaikanal hill stations. Andaman Islands: Havelock (Radhanagar beach), scuba diving, best Nov-May.
